transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get started on the disposition for the 600 totes from yesterday's sanitation cycle. As you know, this batch was cleaned with the wrong alkaline chemical and is currently segregated from normal inventory. Before I approve any disposition plan, I need quality engineering and production control to report any relevant findings. Let's start with quality engineering — what do we know about the impact of the incorrect chemical on the totes?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I completed my swab and rinse-water review this morning. Here's what I found: 140 of the 600 totes have absorbed chemical residue and must be scrapped. The remaining 460 totes can be released, but only after exactly two fresh-water rinse cycles and a final conductivity result of no more than 50 microsiemens per centimeter. I should note that the signed lab worksheet has not yet been attached to the disposition record, so I'll need to get that added before any formal approval.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I confirmed with customer fulfillment this morning that 300 clean totes are required for Monday's 10:00 shipment and the remaining 160 usable totes are required for Wednesday's 14:00 shipment. I received the confirmation in the customer portal, but the dispatch board has not yet been updated.
transcript.speaker: A3
